slides: Okay, before you practice, here's a quick summary of percentages.
Everything important, one idea at a time.
Percent means over a hundred. And "of" means times.
That's the percent formula. Ninety-five percent of sixty... that's ninety-five over a hundred, times sixty. Fifty-seven.
Unknown percent? Unknown whole? It's the same equation. You just solve it.
And you're allowed to swap them. a percent of b equals b percent of a. So eight percent of fifty is fifty percent of eight. Four.
Know these by heart. Halve to go down: fifty, twenty-five, twelve and a half percent.
Then build the families. Seven eighths? Seven times twelve and a half... eighty-seven and a half percent.
Equal ratios, the triangle value. Percents on the left, amounts on the right.
So ninety-five times sixty, divided by a hundred. Fifty-seven.
You can also jump between percents. Twelve percent is thirty? Then four percent is ten, and twenty-eight percent is seventy. You don't even need the whole.
Ten percent? Just divide by ten. Ten percent of three hundred forty is thirty-four.
Then build any percent from ten-percent chunks. And five percent is half of ten percent.
Whole missing? Go down to ten percent, then up to a hundred.
A change is always measured against where it started. The original.
Forty up to fifty? That's ten out of forty. Twenty-five percent... not twenty.
Going backwards? Well, forty-five is what stayed after a twenty-five percent loss. That's seventy-five percent. So the original is sixty.
No starting number? Plug in a hundred. The number you get at the end is the percent.
Now, who is the hundred percent? It's the word after "of" or "than"... in the question itself.
And it can change on the way. Up fifty percent, then down twenty. After the rise, the twenty percent is of a hundred fifty, not of a hundred.
So each new percent sits on the new amount.
A fixed amount in the story? Then a hundred doesn't work. Use the real number, or a letter.
Up forty percent? That's times one point four. Down thirty-five percent? Times zero point six five.
Several changes? Multiply the factors. So down ten percent twice is down nineteen percent, not twenty.
And up forty and then down forty doesn't bring you back to the start. It's sixteen percent lower.
A percent of a percent? Multiply them. That's the percent tree. Forty percent of thirty percent is twelve percent.
Forty percent more than sixty is a hundred forty percent of sixty. So, eighty-four.
Mixtures: find what stays the same. Add water? The salt stays. Add sugar? The water stays.
Letters in the choices? Plug in numbers. Not zero, not one, and a different number for each letter.
And you don't always need the exact number. Estimate, or test a round choice.
So, before you start, always ask yourself these questions.
And the traps: adding percents that sit on different amounts, dividing a change by the new number, and thinking that up and down brings you back to the start.
Okay, now it's your turn. Good luck.
